profile_text.body:
Amira Learning describes itself as purposeful technology built for teachers and educators, designed to help students achieve reading proficiency. According to its site, Amira listens, assesses, and tutors in real time using neuroscience and AI, builds and executes evidence-based AI lesson plans consistent with a core strategy, differentiates for each student's needs, and maps a path to mastery. The site also quotes praise for its AI diagnostic screener, calling its ability to quickly provide actionable data a game-changer.

The company's tracked product is Amira Learning, listed under Education and Research AI. It is described as speech recognition tutoring in English and Spanish, used as an AI reading tutor, fluency assessment, and dyslexia screening, for PreK to 8 students rostered by the district and their teachers. The vendor states COPPA compliance and that student data is not sent to public AI models. District data privacy agreements include a signed example in the SDPC registry with Scottsdale USD in 2024. In June 2026 a Portland board member questioned contract data fields such as place of birth and migrant status, and New Mexico let districts opt out of voice recording. Pricing from a 2024 California state filing lists the screener at $4.99 per student and the full suite at $20 per student, with some states funding free access. The product note also carries a caution that the research is vendor-cited.
